Hera. The queen of the Olympian gods and goddess of marriage, family, and women in Greek mythology. As the wife of Zeus, she is perpetually wronged by his countless infidelities and extra-marital offspring, making her a figure both powerful and consumed by jealousy. Hera's vindictive pursuit of Zeus's illegitimate children, particularly the hero Heracles, reveals her complexity: a wronged spouse whose wrath becomes legendary, yet also a protector of matrimonial bonds and legitimate heirs.

Hera is the queen of Olympus and one of the twelve major Olympian deities, presiding over marriage, family, women, and the bonds of matrimonial fidelity and legitimate heirs. Married to Zeus, the king of the gods, whose notorious infidelities and countless affairs with goddesses, nymphs, and mortals make her marriage eternally tempestuous. Jealousy becomes her defining emotion. She is the mother of Ares, the war god; Hephaestus, the craftsman god; and Hebe, the goddess of youth. Notably, she bears Zeus fewer children than he has with others, reinforcing her sense of betrayal.

Sometimes she is described as the sole creator of Typhon, the most terrible monster in Greek mythology, born from her anger at Zeus. A being capable of threatening even the Olympian order itself. Her persecution of Heracles, Zeus's illegitimate son by the mortal Alcmene, is legendary. She drove him to murderous madness, inflicted the Nemean Lion and other monsters upon him, and hounded him throughout his Twelve Labors.

She is worshipped throughout Greece with special prominence at Argos, and associated with the peacock, her sacred bird; the pomegranate, symbol of fertility and marriage; and the color gold, reflecting her queenly status. Known for her dignity, formality, and strict adherence to proper hierarchy, protocol, and ritual observance, qualities making her both deeply revered and genuinely feared by gods and mortals alike.

She is identified with the Roman goddess Juno, who paradoxically became even more prominent in Roman religious practice than Hera was in Greek religion, reflecting Roman emphasis on civic order and marital law. Zeus is her husband and the source of her endless suffering and wrath. Heracles is her most famous victim, whose torments by her hand became legendary. Hephaestus is her son, whom she sometimes rejected. Ares is another of her children, though he too suffered her disciplinary hand. Marriage in mythology is the institution over which she presides and defends. Olympus is her realm as queen of the gods.
